interest: This document is significant as an administrative record showing the high value the U.S. Department of State placed on firsthand economic intelligence gathered immediately following the outbreak of the Pacific War on December 8, 1941 (Tokyo time). Foreign Service Officer Frank S. Williams, likely interned or repatriated from Japan, compiled financial and economic data under wartime conditions, earning an official 'EXCELLENT' rating signed by Dean Acheson on behalf of the Secretary of State. For historians of wartime diplomacy and intelligence, it highlights the administrative recognition and priority given to repatriated diplomatic reporting on the Japanese domestic economy.
overview: This file consists of a single State Department letter dated September 10, 1942, signed for the Secretary of State by Dean Acheson and addressed to American Foreign Service Officer Frank S. Williams, who was then present in the Department of State. The communication formally acknowledges receipt of Williams's report entitled 'Economic and Financial Notes Compiled from December 8, 1941' and informs him that, due to the high interest and value of the intelligence it provided regarding Japanese economic and financial matters following the outbreak of war, the Department accorded the report an official rating of EXCELLENT.

subfiles.summary: On September 10, 1942, Dean Acheson, writing for the Secretary of State, officially acknowledges receipt of a report submitted by American Foreign Service Officer Frank S. Williams titled 'Economic and Financial Notes Compiled from December 8, 1941'. The report documented financial and economic developments in Japan following the outbreak of the Pacific War. Acheson informs Williams that, in light of the information's significant value and interest, the Department of State has accorded the report a rating of EXCELLENT.
